SUMMARY:
For Q_u(z)=(1+u^2)z^4-8uz^3+(11u^2-1)z^2+6uz-u^2 and every u in Q^*, the rational-specialization types left after audited M3-T11-108 are completely classified. The rational 1+3 locus is exactly one explicit degree-4 P^1 image phi, the A4 discriminant-square locus is exactly one explicit degree-2 P^1 image psi, and the two images are disjoint. Consequently every rational specialization has exactly one of the Galois/factorization types S3(1+3), A4(irreducible), or S4(irreducible). This is exact specialization control, not a Stage37 counting saving.


CLAIM:
Regarded as a quadratic in u,
Disc_u(Q_u(z))=-4z^2(z^2-2)^3.
For u!=0, Q_u has a rational root iff z^2+w^2=2 for rational z,w, hence iff
u=phi(t)
=-2(t-1)(t^2-2t-1)/(t^4-6t^3+12t^2-14t+11)
for some t in P^1(Q), excluding the u=0 image.
In homogeneous coordinates
U_13=-2s(r-s)(r^2-2rs-s^2),
V_13=r^4-6r^3s+12r^2s^2-14rs^3+11s^4,
with Res_r(U_13,V_13)=-4096s^16.
Thus phi has degree 4 and h(phi(t))=4h(t)+O(1), giving ambient count O(H^(1/2)).


The quartic discriminant squareclass is [2-25u^2]. Its square locus is exactly
u=psi(t)=(t^2-2t-1)/(5(t^2+1)).
In homogeneous coordinates
U_A4=r^2-2rs-s^2,
V_A4=5(r^2+s^2),
with Res_r(U_A4,V_A4)=200s^4.
Thus psi has degree 2 and h(psi(t))=2h(t)+O(1), giving ambient count O(H).


Substitution into the discriminant gives
2-25phi(t)^2
=
2(t^2+2t-1)^2
(t^4-16t^3+72t^2-124t+71)
/(t^4-6t^3+12t^2-14t+11)^2.
The homogenized residual quartic F satisfies 2F(r,s) in {2,3} modulo 5 for every [r:s] in P^1(F_5), hence it is never a rational square. Therefore the phi and psi images are disjoint.


Combining with M3-T11-108:
- phi image: exactly 1+3 and Gal=S3;
- psi image: irreducible and Gal=A4;
- complement: irreducible and Gal=S4.

The next useful question is quantitative/physical: whether these images admit an exact same-measure R<=B saving, or whether the generic S4 branch yields genuinely global nonlocal Selmer/support information.

TYPE:

SUMMARY:
On the hostile-audit-passed rational 1+3 exceptional image u=phi(r/s), the physical common-u Gaussian norm factors exactly, up to the already-known 2-power reduction, as
a^2+b^2 ~ Q0*Q1^3
with
Q0=r^2+s^2,
Q1=r^2-4rs+5s^2=(r-2s)^2+s^2.
The two Gaussian norms are odd-coprime. At every interior fresh prime p^lambda with n=2lambda+c_p, exact physical valuation forces either v_p(Q0)=n or 3v_p(Q1)=n. The global rational quartic root vartheta=(r^2-2rs-s^2)/(r^2+s^2) then equals the canonical negative-valuation local root in the Q0 case, while in the Q1 case it lies in the finite degree-3 cluster, forcing the audited cubic-resonant/reducible local branch. Thus every nonresonant interior fresh prime on the global phi image is forced into Q0.


CLAIM:
Let
N=r^2-2rs-s^2,
Q0=r^2+s^2,
Q1=r^2-4rs+5s^2,
U_phi=-2s(r-s)N,
V_phi=r^4-6r^3s+12r^2s^2-14rs^3+11s^4.
Then exactly
U_phi^2+V_phi^2=Q0*Q1^3.


Exact resultants:
Res_r(Q0,Q1)=32s^4,
Res_r(N,Q0)=8s^4,
Res_r(N,Q1)=8s^4.
Together with audited M3-T11-109
Res_r(U_phi,V_phi)=-4096s^16,
all odd cancellation/common support is excluded for primitive (r,s).


Therefore, for every relative-fresh odd p and reduced physical u=a/b,
v_p(a^2+b^2)=v_p(Q0)+3v_p(Q1),
with at most one nonzero term.


For an interior fresh p^lambda, audited M3-T11-106 gives
n=v_p(a^2+b^2)=2lambda+c_p,
0<c_p<2lambda.
Hence exactly:
A. p|Q0 and v_p(Q0)=n; or
B. p|Q1 and 3v_p(Q1)=n, so 3|n.


The global rational root supplied by phi is
vartheta=N/Q0.
In case A, odd coprimality gives v_p(vartheta)=-n, so by M3-T11-106 it is exactly the canonical negative-valuation local linear root.
In case B, N and Q0 are p-units, so vartheta is a p-adic unit and belongs to the finite degree-3 local factor. Since vartheta is Q_p-rational, that degree-3 factor is reducible. Thus case B can occur only on the M3-T11-106 cubic-resonant branch.


Equivalently:
nonresonant interior fresh prime on phi => Q0 allocation and global rational root = canonical negative-valuation root.

STATEMENT.
Let M=M_rel, C=C_u with 0<=v_p(C)<=2v_p(M), and L=M^2 C. Fix M,C (hence L), and restrict physical points to those having at least one primitive psi parameter [r:s] with max(|r|,|s|)<=H, H>=1. Denote their number E_psi(B;M,C,H). Then
E_psi(B;M,C,H) << B^o(1) 4^omega(M) (H^2/L+1).
On the polynomial physical range, equivalently
E_psi(B;M,C,H) << B^o(1) (H^2/(M^2 C)+1).
The B^o(1) factor is the previously audited fixed-u physical multiplicity, not new multiplicity credit.
For a fixed oriented rho modulo L and one choice of the two psi root lines at every p, the primitive parameter count is O(H^2/L+1), with an absolute constant independent of lattice shape.


PROOF.
(i) Audited 111 gives p=1 mod12 at every p|M. Choose the existing common-u Gaussian root rho modulo L. At extreme c_p=2lambda, L uses only the capped depth 4lambda, which is valid even if the actual norm valuation is larger. No unjustified exact saturation is needed.
(ii) At each p^n||L the binary quadratic N-5rho Q0 has exactly two simple projective root lines. A line is the kernel of a primitive covector modulo p^n, including the infinity chart. Selecting one at every p and using CRT gives a primitive covector modulo L. Its kernel in Z^2 is a rank-two lattice Lambda of determinant exactly L: the covector map Z^2 -> Z/L is surjective.
(iii) Primitive lattice lemma. Choose a Gauss-reduced integral basis b1,b2 of Lambda, with |b1|<=|b2| and angle between 60 and 120 degrees. Then |b1||b2| is comparable to det(Lambda)=L. If v=m b1+n b2 has sup norm <=H, elementary inversion gives |m|<=K H/|b1| and |n|<=K H/|b2| for an absolute K. A Z^2-primitive v must have gcd(m,n)=1, since a common divisor divides both integer coordinates of v. For n=0 only m=+/-1 can survive. For n!=0, if such a vector occurs then both H/|b1| and H/|b2| are bounded below by an absolute positive constant. Thus the number is O((H/|b1|)(H/|b2|))=O(H^2/L). Adding the n=0 contribution proves O(H^2/L+1). This is a deterministic upper bound, including highly anisotropic lattices; there is no H/lambda1 error term.
(iv) There are at most 2^omega(M) Gaussian orientations and 2^omega(M) pullback line choices, hence at most 4^omega(M) lattices. Sum their upper bounds. Counting signed primitive pairs overcounts projective parameters by only a bounded factor.
(v) Every counted physical endpoint has a parameter in this set. Each parameter determines exactly one u=psi(r/s); apply audited 036 to bound physical multiplicity for each realized u by B^o(1). Extra endpoint equations and exact R<=B restrictions are monotone post-filters. No ambient density is substituted for the physical population.


HEIGHT AND MOVING-CONDUCTOR CONSEQUENCE.
H is a stated parameter-height cutoff, not an asserted power of B. The exact psi height relation is h(u)=2h(t)+O(1) for logarithmic heights, but no new sharp physical B-exponent is proved here.
For finitely many fixed conductor pairs (M,C) in a shell, with a common valid cutoff H, the rigorous union upper bound is
B^o(1) sum_(M,C) (H^2/(M^2 C)+1).
Duplicates only enlarge this upper bound.
To bound active realized u-values below B^(1/12-delta), it is sufficient to establish that this actual physical-shell sum is O(B^(1/12-delta)), or to replace the separate-modulus sum by a sharper joint incidence bound. Such an estimate is NOT proved.
The +1 term records the thin-lattice / large-modulus occupancy obstruction: when L>H^2, this method gives O(B^o(1)) per conductor pair rather than a reciprocal-L gain that can be summed freely. No physical lower-bound or actual endpoint existence is asserted by this observation.

1. Exact norm and reduction.
Write primitive psi parameter t=r/s and
N=r^2-2rs-s^2, Q0=r^2+s^2, u=N/(5Q0).
Define
F(r,s)=N^2+25Q0^2
=26r^4-4r^3s+52r^2s^2+4rs^3+26s^4.
IMPORTANT_COEFFICIENT=52, not 48.
For primitive (r,s), g=gcd(N,5Q0) is exactly 1 or 2. Odd common divisors of N,Q0 are excluded by the resultant 8s^4; N has no primitive zero mod5. For mixed parity g=1; for both odd N,Q0 each have valuation exactly 1 at 2, so g=2.
Thus reduced u=a/b has
a^2+b^2=F(r,s)/g^2.
The canonical positive squarefree kernel
d=sf(a^2+b^2)=sf(F(r,s))
is independent of the parameter preimage: g^2 and projective scaling are squares.
For H=max(|r|,|s|), |N|<=4H^2 and Q0<=2H^2, hence
0<F(r,s)<=116H^4.
This is a direct height inequality; no physical B-exponent for H is imported.


2. New fixed-d genus-one fiber.
For a positive squarefree d, write F(r,s)=d q^2. Then the parameter point lies on the smooth genus-one double cover
C_d: Y^2=d F(t,1),
with Y=d q/s^2 on the finite chart, and the projective infinity chart retained.
For the binary quartic F, using the same scaled-Jacobian convention as 036:
I=10864,
J=2219776,
4I^3-J^2=201553920000 !=0.
For dF the invariants are I_d=d^2 I, J_d=d^3 J. Therefore
E_d: y^2=x^3-293328d^2 x-59933952d^3
=(x-624d)(x+276d)(x+348d).
For every d>0 the three roots are distinct. Consequently E_d has full rational 2-torsion over Q; in particular (624d,0) has exact order 2.
This family is a rational quadratic-twist family of one fixed elliptic curve, not the old fixed-u or fixed-theta family.


3. Uniform fixed-d parameter and physical count.
Assume H<=B^A for one fixed A, as allowed by the audited polynomial physical range. For realized d, d<=116H^4<=B^O_A(1).
The standard degree-four binary-quartic 2-cover C_d -> Jac(C_d)=E_d, used as a counting interface in 036, has fixed-degree algebraic formulas whose coefficient heights grow polynomially in d. Thus a parameter point of height <=H and Y=d q/s^2 maps to an E_d(Q) point of naive x-height B^O_A(1). Branch/pole/infinity charts contribute only bounded exceptional points.
The model height h(E_d)=O(log d)=O_A(log B).
The canonical-height comparison quoted in Dujella's paper gives canonical height O_A(log B). Choose a single enlarged height parameter T=B^K_A, with K_A fixed and large enough both for the induced point bound and T>=exp(max(h(E_d),e)).
Dujella Theorem 1.1 applies over the fixed field Q with prime order 2:
# such E_d(Q) points <=exp(O_A(log B/log log B))=B^o(1),
uniformly for every realized d.
The covering degree is four, so fixed d gives B^o(1) primitive projective psi parameters in the physical polynomial-height range. Composing each parameter t -> u with audited 036 gives B^o(1) physical endpoints for fixed d and fixed packet. Two subpolynomial bounds multiply to a subpolynomial bound; they are not charged as separate density savings.


4. Joint large-conductor tail — no per-modulus +1 sum.
Let E_psi(B;H,M0) count those exact physical endpoints admitting a primitive psi parameter of height <=H and with their actual M_rel>=M0>=1.
The audited common-u conductor gives M_rel^2 | a^2+b^2, hence M_rel^2 | F(r,s).
Removing the square factor M_rel^2 preserves d and leaves a positive integer, so
d=sf(F/M_rel^2)<=F/M_rel^2<=116H^4/M0^2.
Therefore every endpoint is routed once by its canonical d to one of at most
D=floor(116H^4/M0^2)
positive squarefree integer values.
Applying (3) to each d gives the provisional same-measure upper bound
E_psi(B;H,M0) <<_A B^o(1) H^4/M0^2.
If D=0 the subset is empty. The elementary ambient parameter upper bound plus 036 also gives B^o(1)H^2; hence
E_psi(B;H,M0) <<_A B^o(1) min(H^2,H^4/M0^2).
This sums over all moving actual M_rel and C_u simultaneously. It does not sum 112's +1 over conductor pairs, and it does not assume any distribution or independence of d.
The incremental C_u is not charged; only the already-existing square M_rel^2 is used as a deterministic divisor in a replacement count.


5. Precisely scoped exponent consequence.
On a height/conductor window H<=B^h and M_rel>=B^m, the new bound is
E_psi << B^(4h-2m+o(1)).
Thus a one-twelfth support deficit is obtained for this psi subpopulation if
4h-2m<1/12.
For the hard conductor threshold m=1/12-eta, it is sufficient to have
h<1/16-eta/2.
For example H<=B^(1/16-epsilon), M_rel>=B^(1/12-eta), with 4epsilon>2eta, gives
E_psi << B^(1/12-4epsilon+2eta+o(1)).
This is a bounded-height-window result only. No claim is made that all physical psi endpoints satisfy this small parameter-height bound. The remaining high-height psi region is uncontrolled by this one-twelfth argument.
No primary-gate closure, total numerator improvement or P/M3 limit is claimed.

Every physical psi point has a polynomial parameter-height bound: reduced psi denominator is b=5(r^2+s^2)/g with g in {1,2}, so H(t)^2<=r^2+s^2=g*b/5<=2b/5. ## 1. Integral cofactor with fixed-packet squareclass


Let L=L1*L2*L3, Rrel=tau1*tau2*tau3, and define


W_car=2*L*tau0^6*Rrel^4,
J_car=W_car/N_u.


Audited 115 gives N_u | W_car, so J_car is a positive integer. This symbol J_car is unrelated to the binary-quartic invariant J=2219776. W_car is not the actual reduced denominator D: it is an upper divisibility carrier. No equality D=W_car is assumed.


The core contribution tau0^6*Rrel^4 is a square. From N_u*J_car=W_car it follows exactly that


d=sf(N_u)=sf(2*L*J_car).


Thus for fixed J_car and the fixed packet, d is uniquely determined. Audited 113 gives B^o(1) physical psi endpoints for that d. This absorbs all moving core choices, conductor allocations, orientations and parameter heights; none is charged again. If endpoints admit several retained core representations, union counting remains valid.


For Y>=1 in the polynomial physical range,


E_psi(B; J_car<=Y) << B^o(1)*Y.


More generally an allowed J_car support set of cardinality A gives A B^o(1). This receiver applies to large-Xi endpoints as well: no condition on rad(tau0^sharp)*d_rel is imposed. It does not prove J_car small globally.


## 2. A high-parameter-height window


Write the primitive psi parameter t=r/s and H=max(|r|,|s|). Audited reduction gives N_u=F(r,s)/g^2, g in {1,2}, where


F=(r^2-2rs-s^2)^2+25(r^2+s^2)^2 >=25 H^4.


Therefore N_u >=(25/4)H^4. On any exact physical subset with H>=H0, tau0<=T0 and Rrel<=U0 (U0 is a magnitude bound, not 115's common-core radical R0),


J_car <=(8/25)*L*T0^6*U0^4/H0^4,
E_psi << B^o(1)*floor((8/25)*L*T0^6*U0^4/H0^4).


If the floor is zero this subset is empty. L is fixed in the packet; it may grow polynomially with B and must not be silently treated as an absolute constant. With L<=B^ell, T0<=B^t, U0<=B^r, H0>=B^h, a sufficient one-twelfth window is


ell+6t+4r-4h <1/12.


This complements the low-H windows of 113/114. It is a scoped bound, not a proof that all physical parameter heights are high enough relative to their cores.


## 3. Height-free two-sided covering criterion


Retain 114's S_sq=M_rel*T with C_u=kappa*T^2 and kappa=sf(C_u). Then S_sq^2 | N_u and S_sq^2 | W_car. Define


V_norm=N_u/S_sq^2,
K_car=W_car/S_sq^2.


Both are positive integers, and exactly


d=sf(V_norm),
V_norm*J_car=K_car.


For Z,Y>=1, endpoints admitting a representation with K_car<=Z*Y satisfy V_norm<=Z or J_car<=Y. If both strict inequalities failed, their product would exceed Z*Y. The first subset has d<=Z and the second has at most floor(Y) cofactor values. Therefore


E_psi(B; K_car<=Z*Y) << B^o(1)*(floor(Z)+floor(Y)).


In particular, for polynomial K0>=1,


E_psi(B; K_car<=K0) << B^o(1)*sqrt(K0),


by choosing Z=Y=sqrt(K0). Hence K_car<=B^(1/6-2delta), delta>0, gives a one-twelfth support deficit B^(1/12-delta+o(1)) without any small-H cutoff. This is a union of two replacement counts; no independence is assumed.


Explicitly


K_car=2*L*tau0^6*Rrel^4*kappa/(M_rel^2*C_u).


Do not infer that a large C_u alone makes K_car small: the actual kappa and all common/nonfresh core factors remain. Because S_sq<=M_rel^2<=Rrel^2, K_car>=2*L*tau0^6. Thus this balanced window cannot automatically cover large common-core magnitude. The direct small-J_car window is more general than the balanced criterion.

## 1. Exact integral factorization


Write primitive phi parameters r,s, and put
Q0=r^2+s^2,
Q1=r^2-4rs+5s^2,
N=r^2-2rs-s^2,
K=r^2+2rs-s^2,
U=-2s(r-s)N,
V=r^4-6r^3s+12r^2s^2-14rs^3+11s^4.
The physical branch has finite nonzero u=U/V. U^2+V^2=Q0*Q1^3; vartheta=N/Q0.


Define P(z)=V^2 Q_u(z). Exactly
P(z)=(Q0*z-N)*D(z),
where D(z)=d3*z^3+d2*z^2+d1*z+d0, with integer homogeneous coefficients
d3=Q1^3,
d2=N*(r^4+4r^3s-50r^2s^2+100rs^3-51s^4),
d1=4s(r-s)*(3r^4-17r^3s+35r^2s^2-41rs^3+32s^4),
d0=4s^2(r-s)^2*N.
The cubic D is not the conductor C_u. Its monic version is D/Q1^3.


The exact linear/cubic resultant is
Res_z(Q0*z-N,D(z))=2*Q1^2*N*K^3.
Equivalently,
Q0^3*D(N/Q0)=2*Q1^2*N*K^3.
For a nonzero rational parameter pair, Q0,Q1>0 and N,K are nonzero: their roots in r/s involve sqrt(2), and the infinity value is nonzero. Thus the factors never share a rational root here.


## 2. Integer evaluation support theorem


Let the actual evaluation point be z_phys=a/b=S/2 in lowest terms, b>0 and gcd(a,b)=1. These a,b are evaluation numerator/denominator, not the reduced numerator/denominator of u.
Set
L=Q0*a-N*b,
D_h=d3*a^3+d2*a^2*b+d1*a*b^2+d0*b^3.
The physical negative-square norm gives
L*D_h/(Q0*Q1^3*b^4)=-w^2,
so L*D_h=-Q0*Q1^3*(b^2*w)^2 with b^2*w rational.
Both factors are nonzero on the retained distinct-root physical locus. In particular L is not forced to vanish.


Let delta be the signed squarefree integer representative of L: L=delta*y^2 with y a positive integer. Then
rad(|delta|) divides rad(2*Q0*Q1*N*K).


Proof: take p not dividing 2Q0Q1NK. If p divides b, Q0*a is a unit modulo p, so p does not divide L. Otherwise a/b is defined modulo p. If both L and D_h vanished modulo p, N/Q0 would be a root of D modulo p, contradicting the nonzero resultant. Hence p|L implies p does not divide D_h. The displayed negative-square relation then forces v_p(L) even. This proves the support statement for all such primes, without a local-probability assumption. Bad primes are retained rather than divided away.


With H=max(|r|,|s|)>=1,
|delta|<=|2Q0Q1NK|<=640H^8.
For each fixed parameter pair there are at most 2^(omega(2Q0Q1NK)+1) signed delta labels; in the retained polynomial physical height range this is B^o(1). This is a support theorem, not a count of moving parameter pairs or a new endpoint saving.


## 3. Actual rational difference keeps the denominator


The true difference is
z_phys-vartheta=L/(Q0*b).
In Q^*/Q^{*2}, exactly

Consequently the integer delta support theorem does NOT bound the rational linear etale component solely by 2Q0Q1NK. Odd-valuation primes of the moving evaluation denominator b can enter that component. They cannot be silently discarded or replaced by the phi parameter height.

## 2. Denominator-free finite-prime support theorem


Let S_u be the set of rational primes dividing 2aNDelta0, and S_K the prime ideals of O_K above S_u. Define
K(S_K,2)={ [c] in K^*/K^{*2}: v_P(c) is even for all P outside S_K }.


For every retained physical point,
[beta] belongs to K(S_K,2).


Proof: take p not in S_u. The order Z[alpha] is maximal and etale at p, N is a p-unit, and G mod p is squarefree.
If p divides n, primitiveness makes m a p-unit; beta=N m-n alpha is a unit at every prime above p.
If p does not divide n, beta can vanish only where alpha has residue N m/n in F_p. Squarefreeness means at most one prime ideal divides beta, and that prime has residue degree one. The p-valuation of Norm(beta) is therefore exactly its ideal valuation there. The norm is a negative rational square, so this valuation is even. All other valuations are zero.
This proves the statement, including primes in the moving evaluation denominator n. It is an ideal squareclass theorem, not an assertion that beta itself is an S-unit or a square.


At these odd good primes, the corresponding quadratic extension K(sqrt(beta))/K is unramified. Archimedean signs are retained; no positivity or full local Selmer condition is inferred.

## 1. Primitive global plus vector, with no projection content loss
Put x_i=e_i/R, y_i=f_i/R, d_i=2x_i y_i, S=sum d_i, v_i=S-2d_i. Define A_i=e_i+f_i and w_i=x_i+y_i=A_i/R, so w_i^2=1+d_i.


R is odd: if R were even, sum e_i^2=0 mod4 forces all three edges even. Each e_i,f_i has opposite parity, hence A_i is odd. Also A_i is nonzero: e_i=-f_i would give R^2=2e_i^2, impossible for nonzero integers.


The integer triple A is primitive. If an odd prime p divided all A_i, then f_i=-e_i modp, so 2e_i^2=R^2 for each i. Summing gives 2R^2=3R^2 modp, forcing p|R and then p|all e_i, a contradiction. The prime2 cannot divide A. Consequently gcd(A_1,A_2,A_3)=1: the projective representative has no moving common divisor. In addition gcd(A_i,R)=h_i=gcd(e_i,R): after dividing by h_i, the primitive circle pair C_i,F_i and hypotenuse D_i=R/h_i satisfy gcd(C_i+F_i,D_i)=1. For an odd prime divisor of D_i and C_i+F_i the same circle calculation forces both C_i,F_i divisible; D_i is odd.


## 2. Uniform physical-height equivalence
The standard projective height H_+=H([A_1:A_2:A_3]) is exactly max|A_i|. The upper bound is H_+<=sqrt(2)R. Since sum x_i^2=1 and sum y_i^2=2, Cauchy gives
sum (A_i/R)^2=3+2 sum x_i y_i >=3-2sqrt(2).
Thus
((sqrt(2)-1)/sqrt(3))R <= H_+ <= sqrt(2)R,
and in particular R/5 <= H_+ <= sqrt(2)R.
These constants are independent of content packets. This is a proved pushforward of the physical R measure; it is not an arbitrary ambient-height replacement.

 P_A(Z)=D_A(Z)^2-64Z^2 Q_1 Q_2 Q_3.

## 1. Uniform nonzero factors, no fresh hypothesis
From138, A_i=e_i+f_i are all odd and primitive. Set F_0=sum A_i^2, F_i=F_0-2A_i^2.
Odd squares are1 mod8. Thus
 F_0=3 mod8, F_i=1 mod8 for i=1,2,3.
All four factors are nonzero, and C_A=-product F_j=5 mod8 is nonzero. This holds for all primitive physical signed witnesses, all contents and all charts; no finite-u/fresh theorem is needed.139's square-divisor enumeration is therefore finite throughout the physical population.


## 2. Positive physical directions have S and all v_i nonzero
Use d_i=2x_i y_i, S=sum d_i, v_i=S-2d_i, sum x_i^2=1, x_i^2+y_i^2=1. Positive three edges ensure each x_i>0 and each y_i!=0, hence each d_i!=0.
The134 actual signed-sphere identity gives
 T(v)=(SE+P)^2-S^2 P(4S-P)=0,
 E=sum_(i<j)v_i v_j, P=product v_i.
If S=0, then T=P^2 forces P=0, but v_i=-2d_i are all nonzero: contradiction.
If v_i=0, then P=0 and T=(SE)^2. Since S!=0, E=0. Writing the other roots v_j,v_k gives E=v_j v_k=0. Hence a second root vanishes. The remaining root equals S, giving d_k=(S-v_k)/2=0 for its index, again a contradiction.
Nonzero S on the old nondegenerate branch was already retained in ROUTE41; do not credit it as a new counting theorem. This direct physical proof explains why positivity is essential and permits the next elementary integer exclusion without a new u chart assumption.


## 3. No single Heron factor absorbs the whole squared physical diagonal
Directly, F_0/R^2=3+S and F_i/R^2=1+v_i.
Cauchy gives |S|<=2sqrt(2), so
 0<3-2sqrt(2)<=F_0/R^2<=3+2sqrt(2)<6.
If R^2|F_0, its integer quotient is between0 and6 and is3 mod8, because R is odd and R^2=1 mod8. Thus the quotient is3, forcing S=0, impossible.


Each A_i^2 lies in(0,2R^2], so -2<F_i/R^2<4 (the weaker closed bounds also suffice). If R^2|F_i, its integer quotient in[-2,4] is1 mod8, hence1. This forces v_i=0, impossible.
Therefore
 R^2 does NOT divide F_j for any j=0,1,2,3,
although139 proves R^2 divides their product.
This is an exact same-R set exclusion, not a character probability or a support power bound. It applies to every primitive positive endpoint and each signed face witness. Boundary points with a zero edge can violate full-factor exclusion; they are excluded from this theorem.


Equivalently each gcd(R^2,|F_j|) is a proper divisor of R^2. Do not infer a fixed power gap from properness: the missing prime-power can be bounded while R grows. No uniform R^epsilon split has been proved.


## 4. Noncontent support has a unique four-factor square allocation
